description: Claim adjustment group codes, claim adjustment reason codes (CARC) and common remark codes (RARC) in plain language, for REC-09 (PLT-01, ADR-050). The wording is ours, not the code list's. 'appealable' means the code usually points to something the provider or insurer can correct or reconsider (missing information, coding, authorization, a mistaken payer), not that an appeal will succeed. Review yearly (CMP-06); unknown codes are shown as unknown, never guessed.
source: X12 code lists as published by the Washington Publishing Company; descriptions rewritten in plain language

groups.CO: Contractual: the provider agreed to this, so you don't owe it.
groups.PR: Patient responsibility: this part is yours to pay.
groups.OA: Other adjustment: neither you nor the plan pays it, for a reason given by the code.
groups.PI: Payer initiated: the insurer reduced it and the provider can't bill you for it.
groups.CR: Correction or reversal of an earlier decision on this claim.

2.text: Your coinsurance: your percentage of the allowed amount.

3.text: Your copay for this kind of service.

4.text: The procedure code doesn't fit the modifier billed, or a modifier is missing. Usually a coding error the provider can fix.

5.text: The procedure code doesn't fit where the service was done (place of service). Usually a coding error.

6.text: The procedure doesn't fit the patient's age.

7.text: The procedure doesn't fit the patient's sex as recorded by the plan.

11.text: The diagnosis on the claim doesn't support the procedure. Often a coding error the provider can correct.

16.text: The claim was missing information or had an error, so the insurer couldn't process it. The provider can resend it complete.

18.text: The insurer thinks this is a duplicate of a claim or service it already processed.

22.text: The insurer thinks another plan should pay first (coordination of benefits). Update your other coverage with the insurer.

23.text: Reduced because of what an earlier plan already paid.

24.text: Covered under a capitation or managed care arrangement.

26.text: The service was before your coverage started.

27.text: The service was after your coverage ended.

29.text: The provider sent the claim too late. If the provider is in network, they usually can't bill you for it.

31.text: The insurer couldn't find the patient as a member of the plan.

39.text: Services were denied when authorization was requested.

45.text: The charge is above the plan's agreed rate; the difference is the plan discount.

49.text: A routine or preventive service the plan says isn't covered.

50.text: The insurer says the service wasn't medically necessary. You can appeal, usually with a letter from your doctor.

55.text: The insurer considers the procedure experimental or investigational.

59.text: Reduced under the rules for several procedures or services on one day.

96.text: A charge the plan doesn't cover.

97.text: Included in the payment for another service on the same claim (bundled), so it isn't paid separately.

109.text: This insurer doesn't cover the claim; it should go to another payer.

119.text: The plan's maximum for this benefit has been reached.

129.text: A problem with earlier processing of this claim.

131.text: A negotiated discount specific to the claim.

146.text: The diagnosis code isn't valid for the date of service.

151.text: The insurer says the service was done more often than the plan's records support.

167.text: The plan doesn't cover this diagnosis.

170.text: Not paid when this type of provider does the service.

181.text: The procedure code wasn't valid on the date of service.

182.text: A modifier on the claim wasn't valid on the date of service.

185.text: The provider wasn't eligible to be paid for this service.

187.text: Paid from a consumer spending account such as an HSA or FSA.

197.text: The service needed approval in advance (prior authorization) and the insurer has none on file.

198.text: More was done than the prior authorization allowed.

204.text: Not covered under your current benefit plan.

222.text: The plan's limit on hours, days or units for this provider has been reached.

236.text: The procedure or modifier isn't allowed with another one billed for the same day under coding rules.

242.text: Not done by a network provider.

243.text: Not authorized by a network provider.

253.text: A federal payment cut (sequestration) on a Medicare claim.

B7.text: The provider wasn't certified or eligible to be paid for this service on this date.

B15.text: Not paid separately: it depends on another service that was paid.

M15.text: Separately billed services were bundled together.

M51.text: The procedure code is missing, incomplete or invalid.

M76.text: The diagnosis is missing, incomplete or invalid.

MA04.text: The secondary payment can't be worked out without the primary payer's information.

MA130.text: The claim has incomplete or invalid information, and it wasn't appealed: the provider has to send a new claim.

N4.text: The prior insurer's payment information is missing or incomplete.

N19.text: The procedure is incidental to the main procedure on the same day.

N30.text: The patient wasn't eligible for this service.

N130.text: Check your plan documents for what this benefit covers.

N290.text: The rendering provider's identifier is missing or invalid.

N381.text: Check the provider's contract with the plan for how this was paid.

N479.text: The explanation of benefits from the other payer is missing.

N54.text: The claim information doesn't match what the insurer has for this patient.
